proof_summary: At exponent \(m=39101\), the candidate \(N=201886\cdot3^{39101}-1\) is shown prime using the Lucas recurrence \(U_{k+2}=U_{k+1}-3U_k\): modular calculations force the associated period modulo every prime divisor \(p\mid N\) to be divisible by \(F=100943\cdot3^{39101}\), while that period is at most \(p+1\). Since \(N=2F-1\) and \(F>\sqrt N+1\), no prime divisor can be at most \(\sqrt N\), proving primality and furnishing the required positive exponent.
